bug_semantics: When a host exposes a live CLR object to an untrusted Scriban template, the typed accessor admits a property into its shared member map solely because it has a public getter, then services template assignment by calling PropertyInfo.SetValue without requiring a public setter or rejecting an init-only setter. Reflection can therefore invoke private, internal, or protected setters and can mutate init-only properties after construction; the write changes the live host object and survives rendering. Public non-init setters remain intentionally writable, so the distinct public-setter mass-assignment behavior is not removed by the access-control fix.
flaw_origin: Repository-root commit 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 introduced src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/TypedMemberAccessor.cs with the complete causal pairing: PrepareMembers selected properties by public readability at lines 78-107, while TrySetValue at lines 52-70 unconditionally called propertyAccessor.SetValue. Later renames, interface refactors, nullable changes, and conversion changes preserved that setter-blind mechanism until the 2026 fix.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names author Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com> and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, has the message 'Initial version', contains no trailers (including no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer), and has no bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-7jvp-hj45-2f2m describes the attack path through a CLR object pushed into TemplateContext, identifies src/Scriban/Runtime/Accessors/TypedObjectAccessor.cs TrySetValue as the setter-blind sink, distinguishes public-setter mass assignment from the private/internal/init access-modifier bypass, and records repository-advisory metadata of <=7.2.1 affected / 7.2.2 patched.

History search: git log -L 108,123:src/Scriban/Runtime/Accessors/TypedObjectAccessor.cs at vulnerable commit 34d1cd12632d1c09cb5ca9bd7f7d1f1fef13b74f traces the write path through intervening refactors back to 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589. git log --all --follow -S'propertyAccessor.SetValue(target' returns only that same root commit as the addition of the sink; blame was used only as a lead.

BIC content: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 adds src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/TypedMemberAccessor.cs from /dev/null. Its lines 52-70 implement TrySetValue with unconditional PropertyInfo.SetValue, and lines 78-107 populate the same members dictionary by public getter/readability without setter checks. It is a new source file, not a later move, refactor, revert, backport, or release commit.

Direct-predecessor verification: git rev-list --parents -n 1 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589 returns only the commit itself, proving it is the repository root and has no parent commit. git show renders src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/TypedMemberAccessor.cs as new file mode 100644 from /dev/null, so the vulnerable lines are absent in the empty direct predecessor; introducer_parent is therefore null rather than a fabricated tree or commit ID.

The root commit is broad (284 files / 12,883 insertions), but it is not a squash or merge commit and the validated full public history exposes no parent or member commits to decompose. The vulnerable 114-line accessor file is directly introduced there, so squash_decomposed is false and decomposed_shas is empty.

Fix evidence: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/commit/c7377a60c6e067c97f9ffe0e7821fb5b11f8eb76 (direct parent 34d1cd12632d1c09cb5ca9bd7f7d1f1fef13b74f) adds GetSetMethod(false) checks and rejects IsExternalInit setters before PropertyInfo.SetValue, also rejects readonly/literal fields and restricted/init-only indexers, and adds regression coverage in src/Scriban.Tests/TestRuntime.cs. The source fix is in src/Scriban/Runtime/Accessors/TypedObjectAccessor.cs and its safe-runtime documentation explicitly preserves writes to public non-init setters.

Version-boundary cross-check found an advisory metadata error. Tag 7.2.1 resolves to d45f7f03c3407729da7fe663c180ce780adb9329 and tag 7.2.2 resolves to 29294e1b470039a6e2605d1a9b81b07375bb9d30; both precede c7377a60c6e067c97f9ffe0e7821fb5b11f8eb76 and retain the vulnerable code. The first fixed tag is 7.2.3, which resolves exactly to c7377a60c6e067c97f9ffe0e7821fb5b11f8eb76. First-party release pages corroborate this: https://github.com/scriban/scriban/releases/tag/7.2.2 lists only 390db7fff43b42b22ef5da45625a1ba913a2ce95, 54b781ecdbba3f340d50f7d58bc8f096b36e3c04, and 29294e1b470039a6e2605d1a9b81b07375bb9d30 changes, while https://github.com/scriban/scriban/releases/tag/7.2.3 names c7377a60c6e067c97f9ffe0e7821fb5b11f8eb76 as 'Restrict reflected writes to public setters'. git diff 7.2.2..7.2.3 confirms the setter checks first appear across that boundary.

reasoning: The advisory's vulnerable behavior requires both public-getter discovery and unchecked reflective assignment. The earliest public implementation of both is the repository-root commit 46054810b50b03a6d19cd51886321cbbefa5d589: -L history reaches it, exact-string -S history identifies it as the sole addition of the PropertyInfo.SetValue sink, and its new-file diff shows the getter-only member selection beside the unchecked write. Because the commit is the root, there is no 40-hex parent to report; the parent list and /dev/null diff establish absence before it without inventing a parent. Later commits only transformed the implementation. Commit c7377a60c6e067c97f9ffe0e7821fb5b11f8eb76 directly fixes the access-modifier/init bypass by requiring a public, non-init setter and is exactly tag 7.2.3; repository source history shows that the advisory's stated 7.2.2 patched boundary is one release early. Finally, the exact introducer commit object is human-authored and human-committed with no AI trailer or bot identity, so under the BIC-only attribution rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
